resources.string: Shows a Home Assistant sensor value
Only show when the state contains (optional)
Separate multiple terms with commas — one of them appearing in the state is enough (case-insensitive). Example: \"today\" shows a waste sensor only on collection day. Leave empty to always show.
Enter which Home Assistant sensor to display. You\'ll find all three values in Home Assistant.
The address you use to open Home Assistant in your browser — without a path and without a trailing /.
In Home Assistant: tap your username at the bottom left → \"Security\" tab → at the very bottom \"Long-lived access tokens\" → \"Create token\". The token is shown only once — copy it right away.
In Home Assistant under \"Developer tools → States\", find your sensor — the entity ID is in the first column.
Tip: Only local addresses like http://homeassistant.local:8123 or http://192.168.x.x:8123 use unencrypted HTTP. For external access (e.g. Nabu Casa) always use https.
✗ Server error (HTTP %1$d). Check the token or entity ID.
✗ No connection: %1$s. Check the URL and network.
✗ Local network access denied. Without it the app cannot reach Home Assistant on your home network (Settings → Apps → Permissions → Nearby devices).
Condition met when your presence in Home Assistant is \"home\"
Enter which presence entity from Home Assistant to check. The condition is met when its state is \"home\" (invert it in Smartspacer, e.g. for \"away\").
In Home Assistant under \"Developer tools → States\", find the entity that represents your presence — usually \"person.…\" or \"device_tracker.…\". State \"home\" means you\'re home.
